newsitem.title: USA: US Northeast seen cold but winter milder so far.
newsitem.headline: US Northeast seen cold but winter milder so far.

text.p: Temperatures in the key heating oil market of the northeastern United States will be below normal next week, but the region is stuck in a weather pattern which has created a milder winter so far compared to a year ago.

"So far, the winter has been relatively mild in the Northeast compared to last year because we don't have the same weather pattern," said Mike Palmerino, senior meteorologist at Weather Services Corp in Lexington, Massachusetts.

Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis in Chicago said heating oil demand in New York up through January 1 was below year ago and just slightly below normal. Meanwhile, Chicago's heating oil demand has been above normal and year ago.

"The reason that seasonal demand in New York is not as high as Chicago is because the initial delivery point of arctic air during the early part of the winter has been into the central one-third of the country," said Davis.
Meteorologists said the arctic air loses its bite by the time it gets to the Northeast from the Midwest.

Last year, meteorologists said the arctic air went directly down into the Northeast. Cold snaps in the region last winter were 15 to 30 degrees below normal compared to cold snaps of up to 15 degrees below normal forecasted so far this winter.

In fact, despite colder weather in the Midwest, Paul Handler, president of Atlas Forecast in Urbana, Illinois, expects temperatures from December to February to average normal throughout the country, with cold snaps in between.

Near term, most private forecasters expect below normal temperatures to hit the Northeast by this Sunday and last until Friday, but there is disagreement about how much below normal temperatures will be.
Smith Barney's Davis said temperatures from Sunday to Wednesday could average eight to 16 degrees below normal from Boston to down to Washington D.C.

In the Midwestern region (the Dakotas to Illinois to Texas), he said temperatures could be 20 to 30 degrees below normal. Freese-Notis Weather in Des Moines, Iowa expects temperatures to be 10 to 15 degrees below normal in the Northeast.
But, Weather Services expects cold temperatures to dip only up to six degrees below normal there.
"I expect next week to oscillate from four to six degrees below normal to slighty above normal," said Weather Services' Palmerino, adding Tuesday could be above average.
